label: Roofing
headline_template: On the roof before the next rain.
lede_template: Leaks, shingles, and a look before the weather turns in {city}.

services.name: Leak repair
services.what: Water coming through after rain, a stain that grows, or a drip you can time to the weather.
services.benefit: Stop the leak before the drywall and insulation go with it.

services.name: Shingle replacement
services.what: Missing, curled, or bald shingles that leave the deck exposed.
services.benefit: Close the hole in the roof, not just the stain on the ceiling.

services.name: Roof inspections
services.what: A look at the field, flashings, and vents before you buy, sell, or file a claim.
services.benefit: You hear what’s wrong before the next storm writes the report.

services.name: Flat roofs
services.what: Ponding, blisters, or seams that opened on a low-slope roof.
services.benefit: A flat roof fails quietly. Catch it before the office or unit below pays.

services.name: Gutters
services.what: Overflow, pulling away from the fascia, or water dumping next to the foundation.
services.benefit: Get water off the roof and away from the house.

services.name: Storm damage look-over
services.what: After wind or hail — lifted shingles, bruised mats, or a tarp that won’t last.
services.benefit: A clear list of what’s damaged, not a guess from the street.

process.title: You call the shop
process.body: The number on this page rings them. Say if you see a leak, missing shingles, or storm damage.

process.title: They tell you if they can take it
process.body: Ask if they cover your street and when they can look. After a storm, say so up front.

process.title: They look, then they talk
process.body: Someone should get on the roof or in the attic, then tell you repair vs replace before they start tearing off.

faqs.q: How do I know I need a roofer?
faqs.a: Stains on the ceiling, missing shingles, granules in the gutters, or a leak after rain. If you’re not sure, call and describe it.

faqs.q: What should I do while I wait?
faqs.a: Put a bucket under an active drip. Don’t walk a wet roof. If a leak is over a light, kill that breaker.
